what: External check of the frozen pHRR record exp074 on the firemodels/exp FAA polymer cone curves (Scaling_Pyrolysis/FAA_*.csv: 46 HRR curves, 8 polymers, thickness x flux, one curve per cell). Polymer-level MCC inputs come from the generic tables of DOT/FAA/AR-05/14 through declared conversions (variant P), with a no-conversion fallback (F0). The model is the record exactly as fitted on FSRI. TTI (exp046) is declared NOT SCORABLE and THR (exp045) NOT SCORED (see targets).

targets.pHRR_exp074: SCORABLE, report-only, with declared input conversions (P) and a no-conversion fallback (F0) side by side. 43 of 46 curves have the minimum inputs. PBT-GF (3 curves) is NOT SCORABLE: AR-05/14 gives it no heat release capacity, char yield or heat of combustion, and filling them from PBT with a glass fraction would be invented inputs.
targets.TTI_exp046: NOT SCORABLE. (1) The pinned source has no lab-reported ignition time: the FAA files carry only Time_/HRR_ columns. (2) Deriving TTI from HRR onset is rejected, as in A2 ('never': 5-20 s offset against reported values). Here it would be worse: the HDPE/HIPS/PMMA curves are irregularly sampled, with median steps of 3-69 s and gaps up to 165 s. (3) The 'TIGN-*' DEVC SETPOINT times in firemodels/fds Validation/Scaling_Pyrolysis/FDS_Input_Files/FAA_*.fds are written by generate_scaling_pyrolysis_cases.py from an external, unlicensed package (johodges/materials: materials.scripts.algorithms). Their provenance is undocumented; the generator's own findIgnitionTime is an HRR 0.1%-cumulative-energy rule. The guide's T_ign column is back-calculated from measured TTI. Neither is a lab-reported TTI, and both are banned here as labels or inputs. (4) exp046's log_dT needs the MCC onset (t_onset_bc_C). AR-05/14 has only TGA Td, which would be a new proxy. Route to scorable (human step): pull Stoliarov 2009, Stoliarov 2010, Oztekin 2012 and Kempel 2012 from a library, transcribe their reported ignition times, and write a new config. That config must carry the TIGN prior look recorded below.
targets.THR_exp045: NOT SCORED: its inputs do not exist. exp045 is chi x m''_flux x h_c, with m''_flux = SPECIMEN MASS / SURF AREA (pre-test, weighed). No FAA curve reports a specimen mass. Using generic rho x L would make the prediction chi x rho x L x h_c, a near-identity driven by thickness (THR is already 'not like-for-like' in the record). No THR label is computed.
targets.not_declared: CR and FIGRA (not in this item's record list; FIGRA would also need a documented time zero, which these files do not give).

source.pin_check: The executor asserts that rev-parse HEAD equals each commit above, that git status --porcelain is empty in both checkouts, and that every sha256 prefix above matches. Otherwise BLOCKED.
source.license_and_attribution: firemodels/exp and firemodels/fds both carry the NIST software notice (LICENSE.md). It allows use, copying and redistribution with the notice kept intact. Modified works should say what changed and when, and NIST must be acknowledged as the source. Its 'not subject to copyright protection within the United States' sentence covers work by NIST employees. These cone measurements were made by FAA/UMD, FAA with UCLan, and BAM with FAA, published in Elsevier journals, and reached firemodels/exp through johodges/materials (see curves.provenance). So Dravix does NOT call the curves public domain. It relies on the firemodels/exp notice, redistributes no raw curve (the clones stay gitignored), publishes only derived per-curve values (maximum, time of maximum, sampling steps) with the attribution below, and reproduces no figure or table from the papers. Derived per-curve outputs (experiments/runs/external_faa_polymers/) must carry this line: 'Derived from the NIST Fire Research Division Experimental Database (github.com/firemodels/exp, commit e5de681) and FDS validation inputs (github.com/firemodels/fds, commit 830ba57); changed: per-curve maximum extracted and joined with AR-05/14 inputs, <date>. Measurements: Stoliarov et al. 2009 (HDPE, HIPS, PMMA), Stoliarov et al. 2010 (PC, PVC), Oztekin et al. 2012 (PEEK), Kempel et al. 2012 (PBT, PBT-GF).' Cite the papers: Stoliarov, Crowley, Lyon, Linteris, Combust. Flame 156 (2009) 1068-1083, doi 10.1016/j.combustflame.2008.11.010; Stoliarov, Crowley, Walters, Lyon, Combust. Flame 157 (2010) 2024-2034, doi 10.1016/j.combustflame.2010.03.011; Oztekin, Crowley, Lyon, Stoliarov, Patel, Hull, Combust. Flame 159 (2012) 1720-1731, doi 10.1016/j.combustflame.2011.11.009; Kempel, Schartel, Linteris, Stoliarov, Lyon, Walters, Hofmann, Combust. Flame 159 (2012) 2974-2984, doi 10.1016/j.combustflame.2012.03.012. Cite AR-05/14 for the MCC inputs. Cite the FDS Validation Guide (NIST Special Publication 1018-3; Burning_Rate_Chapter.tex at fds 830ba57) for density and thickness. johodges/materials has no licence: not used, not redistributed. The AR-05/14 PDF is never committed.
source.attribution_note: The guide's Scaling Pyrolysis section cites Stoliarov 2009 and Stoliarov 2012 (Fire Mater., gasification of POM/PP/PA66/PET) for all 8 materials. The per-polymer attribution above follows the guide's FAA Polymers subsections instead (PC/PVC: Stoliarov 2010; PEEK: Oztekin 2012, Victrex 450G, dried; PBT: Arnite T06-200 and PBT-GF: Arnite TV4-261, 30 wt% glass fibre, Kempel 2012). 'FAA polymers' is therefore at least three sources (FAA/UMD; FAA with UCLan; BAM with FAA), not one lab.

column_parsing.header_rule: Regex ^(Time|HRR)_(\d+)_(\d+)$ gives (thickness label, flux label). Every HRR_ column must have a Time_ partner, and every file must have exactly the expected columns (below). Otherwise BLOCKED.
column_parsing.case_match: Each curve is matched to the FDS case of the same polymer with EXTERNAL_FLUX equal to the flux label and |THICKNESS*1000 - thickness label| <= 0.6 mm. The match must be one-to-one (46 <-> 46); otherwise BLOCKED. Expected: labels 3/8/27 -> 3.2/8.1/27.0 mm (HDPE, HIPS, PMMA); 3/6/9 -> 3.0/5.5/9.0 (PC; the '6' column is 5.5 mm in both the FDS file and the guide table); 3/6/9 -> 3.0/6.0/9.0 (PVC); 4 -> 4.0 (PBT, PBT-GF); 4 -> 3.9 (PEEK).
column_parsing.trailing_padding_rule: Each file is a rectangular CSV, so a curve shorter than the file's longest one is padded with trailing empty cells (66 of the 92 Time/HRR columns at the pin). Per curve, the executor keeps the leading finite run of its Time_/HRR_ pair and drops the trailing empty cells. BLOCKED if a pair's finite counts differ, if any NaN lies inside a curve (before its last finite entry), or if a curve has no finite entry. Corrected by the skeptic pass: the draft said 'complete (no NaN)', which a literal assertion would have turned into a false BLOCK.
column_parsing.structure_at_pin: All 46 curves have equal Time/HRR finite counts, no interior NaN (trailing padding only, as above), start at t = 0 and increase monotonically. Steps: PC, PVC, PEEK 1 s; PBT 2.8-3.8 s and PBT-GF 4.0-4.4 s (uniform, 101 points); HDPE, HIPS, PMMA irregular (median 3-69 s, 0.1-165 s), consistent with digitised curves. Whether a curve is one test or a replicate average is not documented at the pin.

polymer_map.rule: AR-05/14 rows are joined by exact name, following the repo's rule in data/v2/ingest_faa_loi.py ('Joins across tables are exact-name only. Ambiguous names get no join'). There are two metadata-based exceptions, both decided before any label.
polymer_map.HIPS: AR 'HIPS' (A-1, A-2, A-5, A-6). FSRI training has 'HIPS' (and 'PlasticC', grouped with HIPS): known polymer name.
polymer_map.PMMA: AR 'PMMA' (A-5 prints PMMA twice with identical values 24.8/25.0/0.99, per the draft's reading. The value used is the CSV's A5_verbatim_row 'PMMA 24.8 25.0 0.99'. The executor asserts that the two rows are identical only when a PDF copy is supplied; see mcc_inputs.pdf_for_executor). FSRI has 'PMMA' and 'Black_PMMA': known.
polymer_map.PVC: AR 'PVC (rigid)' (exception 1). AR lists only 'PVC (flex)/(flexible)' and 'PVC (rigid)'. Rigid is chosen from metadata: the Stoliarov 2010 specimen density of 1430 kg/m3 (FDS MATL, 'Direct') matches AR Table A-3 rigid (1415) and not flexible (1255), and no plasticiser is mentioned. FSRI has 'PVC': known.
polymer_map.PBT: AR 'PBT'. Not in FSRI training: new polymer.
polymer_map.PEEK: AR 'PEEK'. Not in FSRI training: new polymer.
polymer_map.HDPE: AR 'PE HD' for Tables A-1, A-2 and A-5 (exception 2: the row label 'Polyethylene (high density)' is the same material). Table A-6 lists only a generic 'PE', so eta_c = NaN by the exact-name rule (the same 'PE' vs 'PE HD' ambiguity the LOI ingest refused). FSRI has 'HDPE': known.
polymer_map.PBT-GF: No AR-05/14 row in Tables A-2, A-5 or A-6 (Table A-1 has 'PBT-G' Td/Tp only). NOT SCORABLE. Not in FSRI training.

row_sets.not_scorable_3: PBT-GF 4.0 mm x {35, 50, 70}. Listed in tests.csv with reason 'no AR-05/14 MCC row'; never predicted.
row_sets.P_primary_28: HIPS 6 and PMMA 6 (3.2 and 8.1 mm x 3 fluxes), PC 5, PVC 5, PBT 3, PEEK 3. Six polymer groups. Nominal flux bins: ~25 (23-25 kW/m2): 4; 35: 1; ~50 (46-50): 8; ~70-75 (69-75): 12; 90-92: 3. The headline pool.
row_sets.P_out_of_range_6: HIPS and PMMA at 27.0 mm x 3 fluxes. Their cone_mass_per_area (25.65 and 29.70 kg/m2) exceeds exp074's training maximum of 17.507. Reported separately, never dropped.
row_sets.P_hdpe_stratum_9: HDPE with eta_c NaN (6 in range; 27.0 mm x 3 out of range). Predicted under P and reported as its own stratum (per-row table, MAE, bias), never in a P pool.
row_sets.F0_primary_34: P_primary_28 + HDPE 3.2 and 8.1 mm (6). Seven polymer groups. Contains the row label_seen_in_draft (HDPE 3.2 mm / 25 kW/m2).
row_sets.F0_out_of_range_9: HDPE, HIPS and PMMA at 27.0 mm.
row_sets.known_vs_new: Known polymer name in exp074's training: P 22 rows / 4 groups (HIPS, PMMA, PC, PVC); F0 28 / 5 (+HDPE). New polymers: PBT and PEEK, 6 rows / 2 groups.
row_sets.count_rule: Any count different from the above -> BLOCKED, with the per-polymer counts.
row_sets.fsri_duplicate_rule: Plan A6 says to exclude data that duplicates FSRI (the 7 JH_NIJ materials: Black PMMA, cardboard, FRP, MDF, OSB, white pine, white spruce). Here that rule removes no row. No JH_* or FSRI_* file is read. The 46 FAA curves are FAA/UMD, UCLan and BAM tests from 2009-2012, not FSRI tests. No FAA row is in exp074's training data or in cone_replicates_fsri.csv. The finding opendata-firemodels-exp-fpl-faa-jh calls them 'different specimens'. Shared polymer names are handled as known_vs_new, not as duplication. The executor asserts that the exp074 frame it loads still has 191 rows / 65 materials / 64 groups after the FAA run, and that no FAA row is ever appended to it. FSRI rows are read only for step 1 and the label-free gate table.

features.model_features: [heat_flux_kWm2, mcc_peak_hrr_Wg, mcc_char_yield_pct, cone_mass_per_area_kgm2, cone_thickness_mm, density_kgm3, mcc_total_hr_kJg, mcc_t_peak_C, mcc_t_onset_C, log_kpc], as models/v2/phrr_hgb_v4.joblib['features'].
features.heat_flux_kWm2: The flux label of the column (= FDS EXTERNAL_FLUX; assert equal). Executor check: exp074 is a HistGradientBoosting model, and the training fluxes 15/25/35/50/75/100 give bin edges at their midpoints, so labels 23-25, 46-50 and 69-75 bin exactly like nominal 25, 50 and 75. The executor asserts that predictions with nominal fluxes (25/50/75 for those labels; others unchanged) are identical. If they are not, both are reported, with the label-flux one as primary.
features.cone_thickness_mm: FDS SURF THICKNESS(1) x 1000 of the matched case.
features.density_kgm3: FDS MATL SAMPLE DENSITY, one value per polymer, measured on the study's specimens ('Direct' in the guide tables): HDPE 860, HIPS 950, PMMA 1100, PC 1180, PVC 1430, PBT 1300, PBT-GF 1520, PEEK 1300. HDPE 860 is below the usual solid HDPE range; it is used as reported and flagged in the input report, never corrected.
features.cone_mass_per_area_kgm2: density_kgm3 x cone_thickness_mm / 1000. This is DERIVED: FSRI's value is the weighed SPECIMEN MASS / SURF AREA, and no FAA specimen mass is reported. Disclosed in every table header.
features.log_kpc: NaN in every variant. exp074's HGB learned a missing-value route for it (126 of 191 training rows are NaN).

variant_P_primary.mcc_peak_hrr_Wg: 0.5 x eta_c (AR-05/14 Table A-6, J/g-K). Heat release capacity is defined as Q_max / beta (Lyon and Walters, J. Anal. Appl. Pyrolysis 71 (2004) 27-46; ASTM D7309), and FSRI's MCC runs at 30 K/min = 0.5 K/s. The conversion assumes eta_c does not depend on rate; A2 discloses the same assumption (macfp_wood_crosslab.json mcc_ps_check). NaN for HDPE (no exact-name eta_c).
variant_P_primary.mcc_total_hr_kJg: (1 - mu) x hc0. AR-05/14 defines hc0 as the heat of complete combustion of the fuel gases (Table A-5 title; section 5.5.2, PCFC). FSRI's total_hr_bc_kJg is per gram of initial sample, and the fuel fraction is (1 - mu) (AR-05/14 eqs. 47 and 56).
variant_P_primary.mcc_t_peak_C: NaN. No source gives an MCC peak temperature.
variant_P_primary.mcc_t_onset_C: NaN. No source gives an MCC onset.
variant_P_primary.declared_values: peak W/g, char %, total HR kJ/g: HIPS 446.5, 0.0, 37.2; PMMA 287.0, 0.0, 25.0; PC 195.0, 25.0, 17.475; PVC 69.0, 9.0, 16.926; PBT 237.0, 7.0, 22.134; PEEK 77.5, 54.0, 10.672; HDPE NaN, 0.0, 41.6. The executor recomputes these from the sources and asserts equality to 1e-9; otherwise BLOCKED.

features.variant_F0_no_imputation_fallback: P but mcc_peak_hrr_Wg = NaN for every row. No rate assumption; char yield and (1 - mu) x hc0 are kept because they are the same quantities by definition. Reported next to P in every headline row.
features.variant_S2_tga_proxy: P but mcc_t_peak_C = AR-05/14 Table A-1 Tp and mcc_t_onset_C = Table A-1 Td (TGA, generic, +-10 C, typically 10-20 K/min against MCC's 30 K/min). Reported only. Expected out of range against training (t_peak max 519.7, t_onset max 468.7): PC (550/476) and PEEK (600/570). Their count is printed beside the S2 R2.
features.hgb_missing_value_semantics: In exp074's training frame mcc_peak_hrr_Wg, mcc_t_peak_C and mcc_t_onset_C have no NaN. scikit-learn 1.7.1 HistGradientBoosting therefore sends a NaN in those features to the child with more training samples at each split (grower.py: missing_go_to_left = n_left > n_right, so ties go right). The skeptic pass checked this on the saved joblib's 200 trees: every split on mcc_peak_hrr_Wg (193), mcc_t_peak_C (201) and mcc_t_onset_C (226) follows the rule. log_kpc, cone_thickness_mm and density_kgm3 had training NaN, so their routes were learned. This route is mechanical, not learned. Every table that involves a NaN in those features says so.
features.range_rule: For every feature, the training range is [min, max] over exp074's 191 rows, NaN ignored, computed and printed by the executor. Values at draft time: flux 15-100; peak 20.717-748.397; char 0-71.33; mass/area 0.076-17.507; L 0.11-50; density 18-2011; total HR 2.839-42.482; t_peak 234.833-519.667; t_onset 171.533-468.7; log_kpc 8.541-12.38. A row is out_of_range if any non-NaN input lies outside. Under P and F0 the only expected cause is mass/area at 27 mm. Reported-only joint flag: dense_thick = density >= 800 and L > 14.15 mm (the thickest dense training row); expected to flag the same 9 rows.

mcc_conversion_gate.when: Step 2. Label-free; runs before any P or S2 prediction.
mcc_conversion_gate.what: For the overlap polymers with an exact FSRI name and an eta_c (HIPS, PMMA, PC, PVC), r = 0.5 x eta_c / FSRI mcc_peak_hrr_Wg. The FSRI value is the material-level value on that material's rows of the exp074 frame (PlasticC and Black_PMMA not used).
mcc_conversion_gate.pass_rule: median r over the 4 polymers within [0.67, 1.5]. The gate is meant to catch a heating-rate convention error (a factor of 2), not to measure agreement between grades.
mcc_conversion_gate.fail: FLAG: P and S2 are not predicted; F0 alone is reported, labelled as the fallback; the orchestrator writes a blocker.
mcc_conversion_gate.report_only: The same ratios for char yield and total HR (AR-derived vs FSRI), plus the full label-free input table: FAA inputs next to the FSRI rows of HDPE, HIPS, PMMA, PC and PVC.

features.sanity_gates: Label-free; checked before any prediction, else BLOCKED. density 800-1600 kg/m3; L 2.5-30 mm; flux 20-100 kW/m2; mass/area 2-35 kg/m2; P peak 50-500 W/g; char 0-60%; total HR 10-42 kJ/g; S2 Tp 250-650 C, Td 250-600 C. These catch parsing errors. They are not outcome rules.
features.freeze: Write features.json (every per-curve input row for P, F0 and S2, the range flags, the gate output and the polymer map) and its sha256 to the run log before any HRR_ column is read.

models.pHRR_exp074: models/v2/phrr_hgb_v4.joblib: TransformedTargetRegressor(HGB, log1p, expm1), fit on all 191 FSRI rows. Assert that bundle['features'] equals the list above and bundle['target'] == 'peak_hrrpua_kWm2'. A refit of TransformedTargetRegressor(hgb(), log1p, expm1) on train_phrr_promote_c2's 191 rows must match the joblib's predictions on those rows within 1e-6 kW/m2; otherwise BLOCKED. FAA predictions use the saved joblib.
models.step1_reproduce: On FSRI rows only, before any FAA prediction: exp074 must reproduce 0.6113 [0.5155, 0.8376] within 0.002 on the mean and both CI ends (repeated GroupKFold 5x10, repeat-0 material-bootstrap CI), on its record groups (material with PlasticC -> HIPS, 64 groups), as the 'exp' rows of train_blend_round1.py. Otherwise BLOCKED. exp046 and exp045 are not reproduced because nothing is scored for them.
models.environment: python 3.12.4, scikit-learn 1.7.1, numpy 2.2.6, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.16.1 (as used for the records). Run with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.

variants.primary: P (declared conversions; log_kpc, t_peak and t_onset NaN).
variants.fallback: F0 (no conversion: peak NaN as well). Shown next to P in every headline row, on P_primary_28 and on its own F0_primary_34.
variants.S2: P plus TGA Td/Tp proxies. Headline R2 and MAE on P_primary_28 only, with the count of rows that have out-of-range inputs.
variants.rule: Each variant changes only its stated inputs, on the same rows. None is selected, promoted or quoted without its label. Variants are not crossed.

labels.pHRR_obs: Max of the HRR_<L>_<q> column over its finite rows, as given: no smoothing, interpolation or resampling (FSRI's target is likewise a raw max). QA columns: time of the maximum, and the sampling steps before and after it.
labels.units_gate: After the labels are read: every obs pHRR must lie in 10-5000 kW/m2, else BLOCKED (units). This is a units check only; no row is removed by it.
labels.known_bias_disclosed: exp074's target is the replicate mean of per-test raw 1 s peaks. These curves are of undocumented processing (possibly replicate-averaged; HDPE/HIPS/PMMA digitised with irregular steps). Averaging replicates can only lower the max (the max of a mean is at most the mean of the maxima). Coarse sampling of a curve can only miss its peak. Digitisation error can go either way and is not quantified. So the expected net effect lowers the observed max, but this is not guaranteed for any single curve. Stated beside every bias number.

scoring.min_n_rule: R2 is reported for a pool only if n_rows >= 20 and n_groups >= 4. A polymer-cluster bootstrap 95% CI (eval_protocol.bootstrap_ci with groups = polymer, n_boot 2000, seed 0) is reported only if n_groups >= 5. Smaller pools get n, mean obs, mean pred, MAE and bias only.
scoring.pHRR_headline: R2 in kW/m2 (sklearn r2_score) and log1p R2 for P on P_primary_28 (6 groups: R2 + CI) and F0 on the same 28 rows (+ CI); F0 on F0_primary_34 (7 groups: R2 + CI); S2 on P_primary_28 (+ CI). Known-polymer subsets: P 22/4 and F0 28/5 (R2; CI only for F0). New polymers (PBT, PEEK; 6/2): MAE and bias only. Wherever '+ CI' appears, the CI is for the kW/m2 R2 only. log1p R2 is a point value with no CI.
scoring.pHRR_tables: Per polymer, per nominal flux bin (25, 35, 50, 70-75, 90-92) and per thickness class (<= 4.0, 5.5-9.0, 27.0 mm), for P and F0: n, mean obs, mean pred, MAE, bias (mean pred - obs), mean(obs)/mean(pred), and the sampling-step range.
scoring.strata_separate: P_out_of_range_6, P_hdpe_stratum_9 and F0_out_of_range_9: a per-row table plus MAE and bias only. Not pooled with the primary.
reported_only_extras: flux response: OLS slope of log(obs) and of log(pred) on log(q), per polymer and thickness series with >= 3 fluxes (HDPE, HIPS, PMMA at each thickness; PC and PVC at 6 mm; PBT; PEEK), for P and F0
thickness response: OLS slope of log(obs) and of log(pred) on log(L) at fixed nominal flux (HDPE, HIPS, PMMA at 25/50/75; PC and PVC at 75), for P and F0, out-of-range rows marked
exp074 predictions by flux at fixed inputs, to show the HGB step response
the mcc_conversion_gate table and the label-free input comparison against the FSRI rows of the 5 overlap polymers
scoring.rounding: R2 to 4 decimals; kW/m2 to 1 decimal; ratios to 3 decimals
scoring.selection_and_adoption: None. Nothing here is a candidate, there is no incumbent comparison, and nothing is promoted.

procedure: 0. Pin checks for both repos (HEAD, clean tree, sha256 prefixes), confirm the config is committed, then column parsing, curve-to-case matching (46 <-> 46) and row-set counts. Cross-check the AR-05/14 values: loi_faa_polymers.csv (sha256 prefix) vs the declared values; the duplicated PMMA row in A-5 only if a PDF copy is supplied (mcc_inputs.pdf_for_executor; otherwise log 'not re-checked'); and the FDS density/thickness vs the guide table. Apply the trailing-padding rule to every curve, but read only the Time_ columns and the finite-entry counts of the HRR_ columns at this step.
1. Reproduce exp074 on FSRI (step1_reproduce) and run the joblib refit check.
2. MCC conversion gate and label-free input report (no FAA label read).
3. Build and freeze the P, F0 and S2 inputs; range flags; sanity gates; write features.json and its sha256. No HRR_ column has been read yet.
4. Predict P, F0 and S2 for the 43 scorable curves (P_primary_28, P_out_of_range_6, HDPE 9) and the nominal-flux invariance check; write the predictions.
5. Read the labels (per-curve max HRR) and run the units gate; compute every metric and table above; write the outputs.
6. Fresh-context critic pass before any number is quoted in STATUS, a model card or a report.

outputs.script: data/v2/validate_external_faa_polymers.py (to be written by the executor after this config is committed; not written in the draft step)
outputs.files: experiments/runs/external_faa_polymers/{features.json, tests.csv, summary.json}. Changed from experiments/results/external_faa_polymers/ by the skeptic pass to match where A2 actually wrote (that run's orchestrator forbade writing into experiments/results/, which forced a disclosed departure; see reports/macfp_wood_crosslab.md). Nothing under experiments/results/ is written. tests.csv has one row per curve (46): polymer, source paper, file, column, thickness label and value, flux label, nominal flux bin, density, mass/area, AR-05/14 names used, inputs per variant, range and dense_thick flags, known/new polymer, row set, label_seen_in_draft, scorable and its reason, obs pHRR, time of max, sampling steps around the max, pred pHRR [P, F0, S2]. Written with the csv module or pandas, with the attribution line in summary.json and in a header comment of the run log.
outputs.tracker: Outside experiments/results/ on purpose: scripts/update_trackers.py ingests only top-level experiments/results/*.json and would mislabel an external R2 as 'rkf_mean (rgkf5x10)'. Any leaderboard row is the orchestrator's decision after the critic. If the orchestrator orders a different location, the executor uses it and discloses the change in the script docstring and summary.json.

interpretation: Quote as 'external check, firemodels/exp FAA polymer cone curves (7 polymers, generic AR-05/14 MCC inputs, derived mass/area), report-only'. Never SOTA, a win or 'validated'. Never next to the 0.30 bar or exp074's FSRI 0.611 as if comparable.

Five of the seven scorable polymers share names with exp074's training materials (different grades, specimens and labs), so this is not a held-out-material test. The two new polymers (PBT, PEEK) have only 6 curves.

Inputs are polymer-level, so within a polymer only flux and thickness vary. R2 over 28 rows mixes between-polymer differences with the within-polymer flux and thickness response; the per-polymer and response tables are the real result.

The MCC inputs are generic literature values, not measurements on these specimens, and mass/area is rho x L rather than a weighed mass. P relies on the rate-independence of eta_c. F0's NaN route is mechanical (majority child), so it shows how much the conversion matters; it is not a better estimate.
The observed maxima come from curves of undocumented processing, so obs is biased low against FSRI's target definition. Bias tables are not pure model bias.
exp074's HGB is constant beyond its training range, so the 27 mm stratum mainly shows extrapolation behaviour. It is reported for completeness, never pooled.
TTI and THR are not scored. Say so wherever this population is mentioned; never imply exp046 was checked externally here.

This is a separate population. Never pool it with FSRI, MaCFP Wood (A2), the exp054 PMMA cross-lab set, Edinburgh PMMA or any other A6 source (NIST FTT-White, FPL, openbcl, RDG). Never average it with them or put it in one table with them as if it were one test. It never changes a number of record, a model card's record value, STATUS.md record lines or the leaderboard. A side-by-side mention of another external check must carry both labels and say the populations, inputs and model provenance differ.

exit_and_flag.BLOCKED_or_FLAG: Uncommitted config; pin, sha256 or clean-tree mismatch; column or count mismatch; curve-to-case match not one-to-one; declared input mismatch; step-1 reproduction or refit-check failure; a sanity gate or the units gate failing; the MCC conversion gate failing (FLAG: F0 only). Write status 'blocked' or 'flagged' in summary.json; the orchestrator writes the blocker file per the exit protocol.
exit_and_flag.EXIT_5: Not applicable: nothing here is compared with a bar and no number of record can change.

open_choices_resolved: pHRR is scored, with conversions declared (P) and a no-conversion fallback (F0) in every headline row. The plan's 'declare them or skip' is met by declaring.
Peak W/g = 0.5 x eta_c (the definition of eta_c plus FSRI's 30 K/min rate), with a label-free factor-of-2 gate against FSRI's own peaks for 4 overlap polymers.
Total HR = (1 - mu) x hc0, because hc0 is per gram of fuel gases and FSRI's total HR is per gram of sample.
MCC T_peak and onset: NaN in the primary; TGA Tp/Td only in S2.
HDPE has no exact-name eta_c (AR 'PE' is generic), following the repo's LOI ingest rule. It is scored only under F0 in a pool, and as a stratum under P.
PVC maps to AR 'PVC (rigid)' from the specimen density; this is metadata, not an outcome.
PBT-GF is not scorable: no MCC inputs, and filling them would be invention.
Thickness: every FAA thickness lies inside exp074's range (0.11-50 mm), but rho x L at 27 mm exceeds the mass/area maximum. Those rows form separate strata, flagged before labels are read.
Flux: labelled values are used. The HGB binning makes them identical to nominal values (asserted).
TTI is NOT SCORABLE (no reported TTI in the open pinned sources; HRR-onset and FDS TIGN setpoints are banned as labels). THR is NOT SCORED (no specimen mass).
Groups are polymers. With 6-7 groups the cluster-bootstrap CI is coarse, so the minimum-n rule limits where R2 and CIs are printed.
Added by the skeptic pass, before any label: the guide's study-specific combustion parameters (PC, PVC, PEEK, PBT, PBT-GF) are not used in any variant (mcc_inputs.specimen_values_not_used).

Added by the skeptic pass, before any label: no variant substitutes FSRI's own material-level MCC features (the exp054 convention) for the overlap polymers. That would give only 5 of 7 polymers measured inputs and turn part of the test into a same-material-features check. FSRI values appear only in the label-free gate table. Such a variant would need a new config.
FSRI-duplicate rule: no row is excluded (row_sets.fsri_duplicate_rule).
